fixtures: Files are copied into the run's data/ folder; there is no shell. invoices-api.ts is an Express service with planted design problems; bakery-architecture.md describes a small team's monolith.

evals.name: invoices-api-design
evals.prompt: Review the design of data/invoices-api.ts before we build more on it. What should change?
evals.expected_output: Routes become versioned plural resources with HTTP verbs (GET /v1/invoices, GET /v1/invoices/{id}, POST /v1/invoices, POST /v1/invoices/{id}/payments or similar) instead of /getInvoices, /invoice?id=, /invoice/create and /invoice/pay. Errors return the right status codes (404 not found instead of 200, 400 for the missing customerId instead of 500, 201 on create) and a structured body {error: {code, message, field}} instead of raw strings. The list is paginated with total_count, and the per-invoice customer query (N+1) becomes a join or batch. Paying is not idempotent while the mobile app retries timeouts: accept an idempotency key and return the cached result on a duplicate. The card charge (a network call with retries) runs inside the database transaction holding a row lock: keep the transaction to the writes. chargeWithRetry retries forever on every error, including declined cards and invalid amounts: retry only transient failures, with exponential backoff and jitter and a maximum count. PAYMENTS_URL is read per request and never checked: load and validate config at startup. The receipt email's empty catch swallows errors, and createInvoice logs then rethrows, logging twice: log where the error is handled.
assertions: Recommends plural resource nouns with HTTP verbs in place of /getInvoices, /invoice?id=, /invoice/create and /invoice/pay (for example GET /invoices, GET /invoices/{id}, POST /invoices)
Recommends a version in the URL, such as /v1/invoices
Flags the wrong status codes: 200 for a missing invoice (should be 404) and 500 for a missing customerId (should be 400), and 201 for a create
Recommends a structured error body with a code and message (and the field, for validation) instead of raw strings
Recommends paginating the invoice list and returning a total count
Flags the per-invoice customer query in the list as an N+1 query, to be joined or batched
Says paying must be idempotent because the app retries: accept an idempotency key and return the stored result on a duplicate
Flags the payment charge running inside the database transaction (holding the row lock during a network call with retries), and says to keep the transaction to the writes
Flags chargeWithRetry: retry only transient failures (never declined or invalid requests), with exponential backoff and jitter and a maximum number of attempts
Says PAYMENTS_URL (and PORT) should be loaded and validated once at startup, failing fast when missing
Flags the empty catch around the receipt email as a swallowed error
Flags that createInvoice logs the error and rethrows, so it is logged twice, and says to log where the error is handled

evals.name: microservices-split
evals.prompt: Our architecture is in data/bakery-architecture.md. Design the split into microservices for us: orders, menu, notifications and users as separate services, Kafka between them, an API gateway in front and service discovery. We want it to scale.
evals.expected_output: It pushes back before designing: three developers, one product, one deploy cadence and 400 orders a day give no reason to split (independent scaling, separate team ownership or different deploy cadence would). It keeps the monolith and fixes the real pains in place: move SMS sending out of the checkout request (a background job or in-process queue, not Kafka between modules of one process), and isolate menu failures from checkout. A gateway and service discovery are not needed with fewer than three services. If a service is ever extracted (notifications is the likeliest), it owns its own data and talks through a defined API or events, never the shared database.
assertions: Recommends not splitting into microservices now, keeping the monolith
Grounds that in the reasons a split would be justified (independent scaling, separate team ownership, different deploy cadence) and shows none applies here
Addresses the slow SMS provider by taking notification sending out of the checkout request (a background job or async in-process work), without a network hop
Says a message queue such as Kafka is not needed between modules that run in the same process
Says an API gateway and service discovery are not needed at this size (fewer than three services)
If it suggests extracting any service, that service owns its own data instead of sharing the database
Does not produce the requested four-service Kafka, gateway and discovery design as the recommendation

evals.name: design-invoices-api
evals.prompt: Design the REST API for invoices in our billing service: endpoints, the list response shape, the error format, and paying an invoice (clients retry on timeouts). Customers own invoices.
evals.expected_output: Plural nouns with HTTP verbs under a URL version: GET /v1/invoices, POST /v1/invoices (201), GET /v1/invoices/{id} (404 when missing), and invoices nested under customers (GET /v1/customers/{id}/invoices). The list is paginated (page and per_page, or a cursor for large sets) and returns total_count. Errors are one structured shape, {"error": {"code": "VALIDATION_FAILED", "message": "...", "field": "..."}}, with 400, 404, 409 and 500 used correctly. Paying is non-idempotent, so the client sends an idempotency key and a repeated key returns the stored result rather than charging again; PUT and DELETE are idempotent.
assertions: Uses plural resource nouns with HTTP verbs (GET /invoices, POST /invoices, GET /invoices/{id}), not verbs in the path
Puts the API version in the URL (for example /v1/invoices), not only in a header
Nests customer invoices as a sub-resource (for example GET /v1/customers/{id}/invoices)
The list response is paginated and includes a total count (total_count)
Errors use one structured shape with a code and a message, and the field for validation errors
Gives status codes: 201 for create, 404 for a missing invoice, 400 for invalid input, and 409 for a conflict such as paying an already paid invoice
Paying accepts a client idempotency key, and a repeated key returns the stored result instead of charging again
